description: Chapter summaries the reader shows under a chapter's title, keyed by chapter number, per language. Like section headings they are editorial aids, not translation: written from Open Word Bible's own wording, stating what the chapter is about and nothing more, so every language can say the same thing. They use no reader settings. Every summary is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

1.en: Paul greets the church in Corinth and thanks God for the grace given them. He rebukes the rival groups forming around leaders and declares that the message of the cross, foolishness to the world, is God's power and wisdom.

2.en: Paul came to Corinth preaching only Jesus crucified, not with clever words. God's wisdom is revealed by the Spirit, and the natural person cannot accept what the spiritual person understands.

3.en: The Corinthians are still infants, quarreling over Paul and Apollos, who are only servants. Jesus is the one foundation; they are God's temple, and whoever wants to be wise must become foolish.

4.en: Paul and his fellow workers are managers answerable to the Lord, who alone will judge. The Corinthians have nothing they were not given, and Paul warns them as a father, sending Timothy to remind them of his ways.

5.en: The church tolerates a man living with his father's wife, and Paul tells them to remove him. They must clear out the old yeast, since Jesus our Passover lamb has been sacrificed, and judge those inside the church.

6.en: Believers should not take each other to court before unbelievers. The wrongdoers will not inherit the kingdom, and the body belongs to the Lord, so they must flee sexual sin and honor God with their bodies.

7.en: Paul answers questions about marriage and sexual relations, divorce, and marriage to an unbeliever. Each should remain in the calling in which they were called, and Paul gives counsel to those not married and to widows, for undivided devotion to the Lord.

8.en: Knowledge puffs up but love builds up. There is one God and one Lord, so food offered to idols is nothing, yet believers must not use their freedom to make the weak fall.

9.en: Paul has the rights of an apostle but has not used them, so as not to hinder the gospel. He has become all things to all people and disciplines himself like a runner competing for the prize.

10.en: Israel's history in the wilderness is a warning against idolatry and grumbling, and God will not let them be tested beyond what they can bear. Believers cannot share both the Lord's table and the table of demons; whatever they do, they should do for God's glory.

11.en: Paul gives instructions about covering the head in worship. He rebukes the Corinthians for divisions at the Lord's Supper and hands on what he received: the bread and the cup that proclaim the Lord's death until the Lord comes.

12.en: The one Spirit gives a variety of gifts for the common good. The church is one body with many parts, each needed by the others, and together they are the body of Jesus.

13.en: Without love, tongues, prophecy, knowledge and faith are nothing. Love is patient and kind, and it never comes to an end, while faith, hope and love remain, and the greatest is love.

14.en: Prophecy builds up the church more than tongues do, unless the tongues are interpreted. Everything in the church's meetings should be done for building up and in good order.

15.en: Paul hands on the gospel he received: Jesus died for our sins, was buried, was raised on the third day and appeared to many. If the dead are not raised, faith is futile, but Jesus is the firstfruits; the dead will be raised with a new body, and death is swallowed up in victory.

16.en: Paul gives directions for the collection for God's people in Jerusalem and shares his travel plans. He urges them to stand firm and do everything in love, and closes with greetings.
